12 A uniform rectangular board is supported by a frictionless pivot at its centre point P.
R
2.5F
20 cm
P
Q
F
Two forces act in the plane of the board. Force F acts at corner Q and force 2.5F acts at
corner R. The perpendicular distance between the line of action of force F and point P is 20 cm.
The board is in equilibrium.
What is the area of the board?
A
160 cm2
B
320 cm2
C
640 cm2
D
1600 cm2

hints: Notice the $20 \text{ cm}$ arrow is the perpendicular distance from P to the line of force $F$ at Q, so the moment of $F$ about P is $F \times 20 \text{ cm}$.
The $2.5F$ force at R must give an equal opposite moment about P, so $F \times 20 \text{ cm} = 2.5F \times d$ where $d$ is the perpendicular distance from P to the top edge.
Because P is the centre, the $20 \text{ cm}$ is half the board width and $d$ is half the board height - use them to get full width, full height and then area.
walkthrough: The board pivots at its centre P, so weight acts at P and has no moment. For equilibrium the sum of moments about P must be zero, so the clockwise and anticlockwise moments from $F$ and $2.5F$ must balance.

Moment of $F$ about P is force times perpendicular distance: $M_F = F \times 20 \text{ cm}$. This $20 \text{ cm}$ is the horizontal distance from the left edge to the centre, so half-width $= 20 \text{ cm}$ and full width $= 40 \text{ cm}$.

Let the perpendicular distance from P to the line of $2.5F$ be $d$. This is the vertical distance from the top edge to the centre, equal to half the board height. Then $M_{2.5F} = 2.5F \times d$ in the opposite sense.
Set moments equal for equilibrium: $F \times 20 \text{ cm} = 2.5F \times d$. Cancel $F$: $d = 20/2.5 \text{ cm} = 8 \text{ cm}$.
Full height $= 2d = 16 \text{ cm}$. Full width $= 40 \text{ cm}$.
Area $= \text{width} \times \text{height} = 40 \text{ cm} \times 16 \text{ cm} = 640 \text{ cm}^2$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is $40 \text{ cm} \times 4 \text{ cm}$ and uses a quarter of the height instead of the full height of $16 \text{ cm}$.

B.explanation: This is $40 \text{ cm} \times 8 \text{ cm}$ and uses only the half-height from P to the top edge instead of the full height.

C.explanation: Balancing moments about P gives half-height $8 \text{ cm}$ and width $40 \text{ cm}$, so area $40 \times 16 = 640 \text{ cm}^2$.

D.explanation: This is $40 \text{ cm} \times 40 \text{ cm}$ and incorrectly assumes the $20 \text{ cm}$ distance is also the perpendicular distance for the $2.5F$ force.
